subject: LDLT_Factor of covariance parameterunderlying matrix is not positive definite error.

messages.author: 8d4d06c10c4d67c9
messages.subject: LDLT_Factor of covariance parameterunderlying matrix is not positive definite error.
parts:
I have a bit of a complicated model:
The response (y_hat) are N pairs of observations coming from I individuals in T treatments, where these I individuals have C covariates. 
The data have measurement errors (e_hat) in the response, and each pair of y_hat observations have covariance, which is given as a vector c_hat of length N.

The model quantifies an imbalance effect between the pair of observations per treatment (parameterized by a vector nu_treatment of length T), an individual effect (parameterized by a vector lambda_individual of length I), and the covariate coefficients. It also has an intercept per treatment (parameterized by a vector gamma_treatment of length T).
It therefore puts a hierarchy over nu_treatment, lambda_individual, an error for each treatment (sigma_sq_treatment), and the treatment intercept.

In addition, it is a mixture of two normals at the observation level with mixing proportions delta and 1-delta

In the log-posterior computation statement, called by increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(log(delta) + multi_normal_log(y_hat, positive_normal_hyper_mean, sigma) , log1m(1-delta) + multi_normal_log(y_hat, negative_normal_hyper_mean, sigma)))

sigma, which is the covariance matrix of the pair of observations. is constructed at each sampling iteration for each observation n E N as:
sigma_sq_treatment+e_hat[n]     ,     c_hat[n]
c_hat[n]     ,     sigma_sq_treatment+e_hat[n]

Calling stan I get a string of errors of this kind:
Error : 
Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
stan::prob::multi_normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): LDLT_Factor of covariance parameterunderlying matrix is not positive definite. LDLT_Factor of covariance parameterlast conditional variance is -13.2475:0.
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,
but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.
Rejecting proposed initial value with zero density.

I must be doing something wrong and probably also inefficient as I'm not taking advantage of the cholesky decomposition, but I'm not sure how to implement what's given as examples in the stan manual to my problem.

Thanks a lot,
rubi

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] LDLT_Factor of covariance parameterunderlying matrix is not positive definite error.
parts:
You need to check that your constructed covariance matrix actually
is positive definite.

> sigma_sq_treatment+e_hat[n] , c_hat[n]
> c_hat[n] , sigma_sq_treatment+e_hat[n]

My linear algebra isn't the strongest, but I think you
need to keep

c_hat[n] < sigma_sq_treatment + e_hat[n]

That is, there can't be more covariance than the product
of the sds (each of which is the same here by construction).

If this constraint gets violated, the sampler won't be able to move.

We've patched the checks recently, but just for symmetry, which
isn't going to be a problem with your construction.

There's no easy way to do this directly with a Cholesky factor
because you're not estimating a plain correlation or covariance
matrix, but constructing it from pieces. You could factor the
result by hand (it's only 2 x 2) and use the more efficient Cholesky
parameterization of multi-normal.

- Bob

Thanks a lot Bob.

I actually made a mistake in my previous post

The covariance matrix is not symmetric. My correction is:
sigma_sq_treatment+e_hat[n]     ,     c_hat[n]

c_hat[n]     ,     sigma_sq_treatment+e_hat[n+N]

so element 1,1 is different from element 2,2 (e_hat[n] and e_hat[n+N] correspond to a pair).

But as a first step I simply set all c_hat's to 0 and dropped the e_hat's (i.e., no measure uncertainty in the response) so that my cov matrix is simply:

sigma_sq_treatment     ,     0
0     ,     sigma_sq_treatment

but I still get the message:
Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:

stan::prob::multi_normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): LDLT_Factor of covariance parameterunderlying matrix is not positive definite. LDLT_Factor of covariance parameterlast conditional variance is -nan:0.

Since sigma_sq_tissue has an inv_gamma prior and is bounded by zero in my code I thought the simplification I made should guarantee that this covariance matrix is always positive definitive.

Any chance you see anything obviously wrong in what I'm doing?

Thanks a lot,
rubi

> stan::prob::multi_normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): LDLT_Factor of covariance parameterunderlying matrix is not positive definite. LDLT_Factor of covariance parameterlast conditional variance is -nan:0.

I'm not sure how this could happen unless sigma_sq_treatment is 0 or NaN.
This could happen with ill-formed inits.
> Since sigma_sq_tissue has an inv_gamma prior and is bounded by zero in my code I thought the simplification I made should guarantee that this covariance matrix is always positive definitive.
The prior doesn't matter.
> Any chance you see anything obviously wrong in what I'm doing

The best thing to do at this point is to print out the
matrix before you call the sampling statement to make sure it's
what you think it is.

If that doesn't yield any insight, try simplifying down just
to something that'll cause the error. It's hard to debug
programs this big.

Does the problem occur right away or later on in sampling?

In the actual model you sent, e_hat is unconstrained and you
add it to the diagonal, so you could get sigma[1,1] < 0, which
isn't going to be positive definite.

If you really reduced it to just sigma_sq_treatment terms on
the diagonal (and zero off diagonal), it should work.
Another potential problem is too great a difference between
the sigmas --- if things are too badly conditioned, linear
algebra can break down.

- Bob
